items.title: Maybe Sunday
items.text:
Pia: Noah, a new comedy is showing tonight. Do you want to come with me?
Noah: Thanks for asking, Pia, but I can't go tonight.
Pia: Oh, do you have other plans?
Noah: Not exactly. I have a math test tomorrow morning, and I'm still confused about the last chapter.
Pia: That sounds stressful. Is it really that hard?
Noah: It is for me. If I go out, I'll just worry about it the whole time.
Pia: I understand. I finished that chapter last week. Would you like some help at lunch today?
Noah: Really? That would be great.
Pia: Sure. The movie is on until next week, so we can go on Sunday.
Noah: Perfect. I'll buy the popcorn.

qs.q: Why does Noah decline Pia's invitation?
o: He has to help with housework
He is upset with Pia
He needs to get ready for a test
He has already seen the movie with other friends
qs.why: Noah는 내일 아침 수학 시험이 있어서 영화를 못 간다고 했어요(math test tomorrow morning).

qs.q: What does Noah mean by "I'll just worry about it the whole time"?
o: He is afraid of the dark theater
He thinks the ticket is too costly
He would not enjoy the movie
He may arrive late to the movie
qs.why: 나가면 시험 걱정만 할 테니 영화를 즐기지 못할 것이라는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: How does Pia respond to Noah's refusal?
o: She feels hurt and stops talking
She is surprised and asks for a reason
She is annoyed and goes alone
She is understanding and offers help
qs.why: Pia는 'I understand'라고 하며 점심 때 도와주겠다고 해요.

qs.q: In the dialogue, the word "confused" is closest in meaning to
o: not clear about something
proud of something
bored with something
tired of something
qs.why: confused는 마지막 단원을 잘 이해하지 못해 헷갈린다는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: How does the conversation end?
o: Noah will join tonight after studying one hour
Pia will help today, and they will see the film later
Pia will see the film alone and tell Noah the story
They cancel their plans and ask a teacher for extra help tonight
qs.why: Pia가 점심에 도와주고 영화는 일요일에 보기로 했어요.

items.title: A Dented Bottle
items.text:
Agent: Thank you for calling Hillside Outdoor Store. How can I help you?
Eli: Hello. I ordered a steel water bottle last week. It came this morning, but the side is badly dented.
Agent: I'm sorry to hear that. Did the box look damaged too?
Eli: Yes, one corner was crushed. I think it happened during delivery.
Agent: Thank you for telling me. I can send you a new bottle, or I can return your money.
Eli: Which is faster?
Agent: A refund takes about three days. A new bottle takes ten days, because the blue one is almost sold out.
Eli: I'm going hiking this Saturday, so I'll take the refund and buy one at a shop nearby.
Agent: Of course. Please send me a photo of the box, and I'll start the refund now.
Eli: I'll send it in a minute. Thanks for your help.

qs.q: What does the agent ask Eli to send?
o: The delivery driver's name
A picture of the box
A copy of the receipt
The damaged bottle
qs.why: 상담원은 박스 사진(a photo of the box)을 보내 달라고 했어요.

qs.q: What can be inferred about a replacement bottle?
o: It would come without a box
It would cost more than the first one
It would be a different color
It would arrive after Eli's trip
qs.why: 새 병은 10일 걸리는데 Eli는 이번 토요일에 등산을 가니 늦어요.

qs.q: How does the agent treat Eli?
o: Nervously and carelessly
Strictly and angrily
Coldly and impatiently
Politely and helpfully
qs.why: 상담원은 사과하고(I'm sorry) 두 가지 해결책을 친절하게 제시했어요.

qs.q: What does "almost sold out" mean?
o: Very few are left to buy
It is too old to sell
It is no longer made
The price is too high
qs.why: sold out은 다 팔렸다는 뜻이라 almost sold out은 거의 남지 않았다는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: What will Eli probably do next?
o: Return the bottle to the store in person
Cancel the hiking trip
Send the photo and buy a bottle somewhere else
Wait ten days for the blue bottle to come from the warehouse
qs.why: Eli는 환불을 받고 근처 가게에서 병을 사겠다고 했어요.

items.title: Behind the Cafeteria Door
items.text:
Haru: Welcome to Room Nine Radio. Today I'm talking with Ms. Lopez, who cooks our school lunches.
Ms. Lopez: Thank you for inviting me, Haru.
Haru: First, what time does your day begin?
Ms. Lopez: Quite early. I arrive at six, because the soup has to cook for hours.
Haru: Wow. What is the hardest part of your job?
Ms. Lopez: Choosing a menu that everyone enjoys. Some students love spicy food, but others can't eat it at all.
Haru: Do you ever change a recipe because of student ideas?
Ms. Lopez: Often! Last term a student suggested adding corn to the rice, and now it's one of our most popular dishes.
Haru: That's wonderful. Do you have a message for our listeners?
Ms. Lopez: Please try one new food each month. You may be surprised.

qs.q: Why does Ms. Lopez arrive at the school early?
o: She must clean the cafeteria
She has to attend a morning meeting
The students eat breakfast at school
The soup needs a long time to cook
qs.why: 수프를 몇 시간 끓여야 해서(the soup has to cook for hours) 일찍 와요.

qs.q: What can be inferred from the story about the corn rice?
o: She dislikes changing old recipes even when students ask her to
Corn is the cheapest food to buy
She sometimes uses students' suggestions
Most students ask for new dishes
qs.why: 학생의 아이디어로 옥수수밥을 만들어 인기 메뉴가 되었으니 학생 의견을 반영한다는 것을 알 수 있어요.

qs.q: Why does Ms. Lopez ask listeners to try a new food each month?
o: She is looking for new recipe ideas
She wants them to be open to new tastes
She needs more students to eat lunch
She wants to sell more corn rice
qs.why: 'You may be surprised'라며 새로운 음식에 열린 마음을 갖기를 바라는 거예요.

qs.q: In the dialogue, "popular" is closest in meaning to
o: made very quickly
good for health
hard to find
liked by many people
qs.why: popular dish는 많은 학생이 좋아하는 요리라는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: Which sentence best sums up the interview?
o: A teacher explains new rules for school lunch
A school cook talks about her work and her menu choices
A reporter teaches listeners how to cook soup
Students argue about which school food is the tastiest and cheapest
qs.why: 급식 조리사가 하루 일과와 메뉴 고민을 이야기하는 인터뷰예요.

items.title: Slow Down, Please
items.text:
Mr. Brown: Thanks for practicing your speech with me, Yuna. Shall we talk about it?
Yuna: Yes, please. Was it okay?
Mr. Brown: The opening was excellent. Your story about the lost kitten made everyone want to listen.
Yuna: I'm glad. I was really nervous, though.
Mr. Brown: It didn't show much. Your eye contact was strong. But you spoke very quickly in the middle, and some words were hard to catch.
Yuna: I think I rushed because I was afraid of forgetting my lines.
Mr. Brown: That's common. Try pausing after each main point. A short pause gives the audience time to think.
Yuna: I'll mark the pauses on my paper with a pencil.
Mr. Brown: Good idea. Practice that way twice tonight, and tomorrow it will feel natural.

qs.q: Which problem does Mr. Brown point out?
o: Yuna forgot the end of her speech and had to start over
Yuna talked too fast in the middle
Yuna did not look at the audience
Yuna's story was too long
qs.why: 중간 부분에서 매우 빠르게 말했다고(spoke very quickly in the middle) 지적해요.

qs.q: What can be inferred about Yuna's nervousness?
o: It disappeared after the opening
It made her stop in the middle and begin the story again
The audience could hardly see it
It was caused by Mr. Brown
qs.why: 'It didn't show much'라고 했으니 긴장이 겉으로 많이 드러나지 않았어요.

qs.q: Why does Mr. Brown suggest pausing after each main point?
o: To give listeners time to think
To let Yuna check her watch
To hide a mistake in the story
To make the speech much longer
qs.why: 잠깐 멈추면 청중이 생각할 시간을 갖게 된다고 설명해요.

qs.q: In the dialogue, "hard to catch" means
o: hard to carry
hard to hear clearly
hard to write down
hard to remember
qs.why: 너무 빨리 말해서 단어가 또렷이 들리지 않았다는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: What will Yuna probably do tonight?
o: Ask Mr. Brown to read it for her
Skip practice to keep calm
Mark pauses on her paper and practice twice
Write a completely new speech with a funnier opening
qs.why: Yuna는 종이에 쉬는 곳을 표시하고 두 번 연습하기로 했어요.

items.title: Train or Car?
items.text:
Jun: Dad says we should drive to Grandpa's house this weekend. What do you think, Sora?
Sora: Driving is faster, but there's always traffic on Saturday mornings.
Jun: True. The train takes two hours, though. That's a whole hour longer.
Sora: Yes, but the train is cheaper, and we can read or play cards.
Jun: Dad doesn't like carrying heavy bags up the station stairs.
Sora: Then we could pack lighter. Grandpa has blankets and towels already.
Jun: Hmm. What about leaving very early by car? Then we'd miss the traffic.
Sora: Mom wouldn't enjoy waking up at five. She stays up late on Fridays.
Jun: Good point. I'll tell Dad we prefer the train if we bring one small bag each.
Sora: Great. I'll make a list of what to leave at home.

qs.q: How much longer does the train trip take than driving?
o: Thirty minutes
Two hours
Three hours
One hour
qs.why: Jun이 기차는 'a whole hour longer'라고 말했어요.

qs.q: What can be inferred about Grandpa's house?
o: It has no heavy furniture inside
It is too small for the whole family to stay overnight
Guests can sleep there without bringing bedding
It is very close to the train station
qs.why: 할아버지 댁에 담요와 수건이 이미 있으니 침구를 가져갈 필요가 없어요.

qs.q: Why does Sora mention that Mom stays up late on Fridays?
o: To complain about a late dinner
To argue against leaving very early
To explain why Mom likes the train
To ask for a different weekend
qs.why: 엄마가 금요일에 늦게 자니 새벽 5시 출발은 좋지 않다는 반대 의견이에요.

qs.q: What does "pack lighter" mean?
o: Pack the bags before dark
Put everything in one large box
Bring fewer and less heavy things
Choose bags of a brighter color
qs.why: pack lighter는 짐을 더 가볍게 싸는 것을 뜻해요.

qs.q: What will Jun most likely tell Dad?
o: They want to drive at five in the morning to avoid traffic
They plan to take the highway after lunch
They would like to go by train with small bags
They will stay home this weekend
qs.why: Jun은 가방을 하나씩만 들고 기차를 타자고 아빠에게 말하겠다고 해요.

items.title: Robots or Beans?
items.text:
Kai: Our science club has fifty dollars left this term. Should we buy a robot kit or start a plant project?
Lena: The robot kit costs forty-eight dollars. That would use nearly everything.
Omar: But robots are exciting. More students might join.
Lena: Maybe. But a plant project is cheaper, and we could use the school courtyard.
Omar: The problem is that plants grow slowly. We might not see results before the science fair.
Kai: Beans grow fast, though. In three weeks we'd have tall plants.
Lena: And we could measure them every Friday and make a chart.
Omar: Okay, that sounds like real science. With the extra money, we could buy a small kit next term.
Kai: Then let's vote. Who wants beans?
Lena: Me.
Omar: Me too.

qs.q: How much does the robot kit cost?
o: Forty-eight dollars
Fifty dollars
Fifteen dollars
Eighteen dollars
qs.why: Lena가 로봇 키트가 48달러(forty-eight dollars)라고 말해요.

qs.q: What can be inferred about Omar's first opinion of the plant project?
o: He believed it had no place at school
He doubted it would give results in time
He thought the project would cost more than the robot kit
He wanted to measure plants every day
qs.why: Omar는 식물이 천천히 자라 과학 발표 전에 결과를 못 볼 수 있다고 걱정했어요.

qs.q: Why does Kai say, "Then let's vote"?
o: To show that the money is gone
To end the talk with a group decision
To ask Omar to leave the club
To stop Lena from speaking any further about the courtyard
qs.why: 의견이 모였으니 투표로 결정을 내리자는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: In "That would use nearly everything," the word "nearly" is closest to
o: exactly
almost
quickly
hardly
qs.why: nearly는 '거의'라는 뜻으로 almost와 같아요.

qs.q: What will the club probably do?
o: Cancel the science fair project
Grow beans now and consider a kit later
Buy the robot kit this week with all of the money
Spend all the money on a courtyard
qs.why: 콩 프로젝트를 하고 남는 돈으로 다음 학기에 작은 키트를 살 수 있다고 했어요.

items.title: One Month on Trial
items.text:
Hana: Dad, I'd like to take guitar lessons at the community center.
Dad: Guitar? You stopped piano after two months.
Hana: I know. Piano was my sister's idea, not mine. This time I chose it myself.
Dad: Lessons cost money, and a guitar is another expense.
Hana: The center lends guitars for free. The lessons are twenty dollars a month.
Dad: And when will you practice? Your homework takes a lot of time.
Hana: Thirty minutes after dinner. I'll even write it on the calendar.
Dad: Hmm. What if you lose interest again?
Hana: Then I'll pay half of the lessons from my allowance. That's a promise.
Dad: All right. Let's try one month first.

qs.q: How can Hana get a guitar without buying one?
o: She can rent one from a music shop
She can ask a friend to give one
She can borrow one from the center
She can use the guitar her sister left at home
qs.why: 센터가 기타를 무료로 빌려준다고(lends guitars for free) 했어요.

qs.q: Why does Dad mention the piano?
o: He believes the piano is too loud
He worries Hana may quit again
He wants Hana to play it again
He thinks Hana's sister should teach her
qs.why: 피아노를 두 달 만에 그만뒀던 일을 말하며 또 그만둘까 걱정해요.

qs.q: Why does Hana offer to pay half from her allowance?
o: To get a bigger allowance from Dad next month
To avoid practicing at home
To make Dad choose a cheaper class
To show she is serious about the plan
qs.why: 용돈으로 절반을 내겠다는 약속은 진지하다는 것을 보여 주려는 거예요.

qs.q: In the dialogue, "lose interest" means
o: lose some money
forget a promise
feel too tired to walk
stop caring about something
qs.why: lose interest는 흥미를 잃는다는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: What is Dad's final decision?
o: He allows lessons for a trial month
He tells Hana to choose piano instead
He refuses until Hana's grades improve
He says Hana must pay for everything
qs.why: Dad는 'Let's try one month first'라며 한 달 시험 삼아 허락해요.

items.title: A Book for Theo
items.text:
Librarian: Hi, Theo. Looking for something today?
Theo: Not really. My teacher told us to borrow a book, but I don't enjoy reading. Books are too long.
Librarian: I hear that a lot. What do you like to do in your free time?
Theo: Mostly basketball and drawing.
Librarian: Then why not try this graphic novel about a girl who invents new basketball tricks? It has lots of pictures, and each chapter takes about ten minutes.
Theo: Pictures help, I guess. But is it funny? I don't want something serious.
Librarian: Very funny. Many students returned it with big smiles. If you don't like chapter one, bring it back and I'll find another.
Theo: That's fair. I'll give it a try.
Librarian: Wonderful. You can check it out at the front desk.

qs.q: Why does Theo say he does not enjoy reading?
o: He cannot find books about sports
He has no time after basketball
He is not allowed in the library
He thinks books are too long
qs.why: Theo는 책이 너무 길다고(Books are too long) 말해요.

qs.q: What can be inferred about the graphic novel?
o: It is a very serious story
Other students have liked it
It is written for younger children
It has never been borrowed
qs.why: 많은 학생이 웃으며 반납했다고 하니 다른 학생들이 재미있게 읽었어요.

qs.q: Why does the librarian say, "bring it back and I'll find another"?
o: To let Theo try the book without pressure
To tell Theo to hurry up and finish the book this week
To say the library has few books
To warn Theo about a late fee
qs.why: 마음에 안 들면 바꿔 주겠다는 말로 부담 없이 읽어 보게 하려는 거예요.

qs.q: In the dialogue, "give it a try" means
o: to test it and see
to hand it to someone
to try on clothes
to return it quickly
qs.why: give it a try는 한번 시도해 본다는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: What will Theo probably do next?
o: Leave the library without a book and ask the teacher for help
Ask for a longer novel
Borrow the book and read the first chapter
Draw a picture for the librarian
qs.why: Theo는 해 보겠다고 했고 사서는 대출 데스크를 안내했어요.

items.title: Volunteer Interview
items.text:
Ms. Reed: Come in, Minho. Please sit down. Thank you for applying to volunteer at our weekend reading program.
Minho: Thank you for seeing me.
Ms. Reed: Why do you want to join?
Minho: Last year my younger cousin couldn't read well, and a volunteer helped. The improvement was huge. I'd like to do the same for other kids.
Ms. Reed: That's a good reason. Have you worked with children before?
Minho: Only my cousin. But I'm patient, and I learn quickly.
Ms. Reed: Patience matters most. The sessions are Saturdays from ten to noon. Can you come every week?
Minho: I have a soccer game once a month, but I can arrive late on those days.
Ms. Reed: That's fine. Just tell us in advance. We'll call you this week.

qs.q: What does Minho say about his soccer game?
o: It happens once a month
It will end before ten
It takes place every Saturday
It is held on Sunday mornings
qs.why: 한 달에 한 번 경기가 있다고(once a month) 해요.

qs.q: What can be inferred about Minho's experience?
o: He has never helped his cousin
He has little experience with children
He has led a club at school
He has taught reading to many children for years
qs.why: 아이들과 일해 본 경험은 사촌뿐이라고(Only my cousin) 했어요.

qs.q: Why does Minho tell the story about his cousin?
o: To explain why he is late
To ask for a favor for his cousin
To show why he wants to volunteer
To prove he is a fast reader and a hard worker
qs.why: 자원봉사자의 도움으로 사촌이 좋아진 경험이 지원 동기예요.

qs.q: In the dialogue, "in advance" means
o: at a long distance
with great care
before something happens
after a short time
qs.why: in advance는 미리, 사전에라는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: What will probably happen after the interview?
o: Ms. Reed will ask Minho to quit soccer
Ms. Reed will offer Minho a volunteer position
Minho will be moved to a weekday program
Minho will be asked to gain more experience first
qs.why: 분위기가 긍정적이고 이번 주에 연락하겠다고 하니 자리를 제안할 가능성이 커요.

items.title: Tired Eyes
items.text:
Dr. Han: Hello, Tomas. What brings you in today?
Tomas: I've been getting headaches in the afternoon for about two weeks.
Dr. Han: Does anything make them better or worse?
Tomas: They're worse after I play video games. I usually play for around four hours after school.
Dr. Han: I see. How much water do you drink?
Tomas: Not much, to be honest. Maybe one glass a day.
Dr. Han: Looking at a screen so long can tire your eyes, and little water may play a part too. Please rest your eyes for ten minutes every hour and drink more water.
Tomas: Do I have to stop gaming completely?
Dr. Han: No, but let's limit it to two hours. If the headaches continue, come back and we'll do more tests.
Tomas: Okay. I'll try that.

qs.q: When do Tomas's headaches get worse?
o: After he plays video games
While he sleeps at night
When he walks to school
Before he eats lunch
qs.why: 게임을 한 뒤에 더 심해진다고(worse after I play video games) 말해요.

qs.q: What does Dr. Han think is behind the headaches?
o: Loud noise at school
Long screen time and little water
A lack of sleep and exercise
Too much homework
qs.why: 화면을 오래 보는 것과 물을 적게 마시는 것을 원인으로 봐요.

qs.q: Why does Dr. Han say, "come back and we'll do more tests"?
o: To scare Tomas into giving up video games for good
To collect payment for the visit
To end the visit quickly
To check again if the advice does not work
qs.why: 두통이 계속되면 다시 와서 검사를 하자는 것이라 조언이 효과가 없을 때를 대비한 말이에요.

qs.q: In the dialogue, "play a part" means
o: be one of the causes
come at the right time
take a seat nearby
act in a school play
qs.why: play a part는 어떤 일에 영향을 미치다, 한 원인이 되다는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: What will Tomas probably do after the visit?
o: Switch to a different school
Stop playing games forever and avoid all screens at home
Cut his gaming time and take eye breaks
Drink only juice with meals
qs.why: 게임을 2시간으로 줄이고 눈을 쉬게 하며 물을 더 마시기로 했어요.

items.title: A Quieter Room
items.text:
Guest: Excuse me, I'm in room 408. Could I talk to you about the noise?
Clerk: Of course. What seems to be the problem?
Guest: Construction work next door started at seven this morning, and the sound comes right through my window.
Clerk: I apologize. Work on the neighboring building begins early. Rooms on the south side are much quieter.
Guest: Are any available?
Clerk: One on the fifth floor, but it faces the parking lot instead of the sea.
Guest: I don't mind. I only need to sleep well tonight because I have an early bus tour tomorrow.
Clerk: I'll move you right away, and a staff member will carry your bags.
Guest: Thank you. That's very kind.
Clerk: Breakfast tomorrow is free for the trouble.

qs.q: What is different about the new room?
o: It has a larger bed
It is on a higher floor than 408
It looks out on the parking lot
It is next to the front desk
qs.why: 새 방은 바다 대신 주차장 쪽이에요(faces the parking lot instead of the sea).

qs.q: What does the guest care about most?
o: Having a beautiful view of the sea from the window
Eating breakfast early
Getting a good night's sleep
Saving money on the room
qs.why: 'I don't mind. I only need to sleep well'이라며 전망보다 숙면을 우선해요.

qs.q: Why does the clerk offer free breakfast?
o: To thank the guest for staying long
To advertise the hotel restaurant
To get the guest to leave early
To make up for the guest's trouble
qs.why: 'for the trouble', 즉 불편을 끼친 것에 대한 보상이에요.

qs.q: In the dialogue, "I don't mind" means
o: I am not listening
I do not remember
it does not bother me
it is not my business
qs.why: I don't mind는 신경 쓰지 않는다, 괜찮다는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: What will happen next?
o: The clerk will bring the bags to the bus
The guest will move to a quieter room
The construction will stop today
The guest will leave the hotel
qs.why: 직원이 바로 조용한 방으로 옮겨 주고 짐도 들어 준다고 했어요.

items.title: Our Class Pet
items.text:
Ms. Ahn: Let's decide on our class pet. Jiho, what do you think?
Jiho: A hamster. It's small and doesn't need much space.
Dana: But hamsters sleep during the day and play at night. We'd hardly see it.
Jiho: Good point. Then fish would be better. They're active in the daytime.
Ms. Ahn: Fish are lovely, but who will feed them on weekends when school is closed?
Dana: I could take the tank home every Friday.
Ms. Ahn: Moving a heavy tank is risky. But a feeder machine can drop food on a timer.
Jiho: Then the fish can stay here!
Dana: That solves everything. I vote for fish.
Ms. Ahn: Good. Let's ask the class to vote on fish with a feeder.

qs.q: Why does Dana object to a hamster?
o: It needs a very large cage
It cannot be fed on weekends
It is awake mostly at night
It is too expensive to keep
qs.why: 햄스터는 낮에 자고 밤에 놀아서 거의 볼 수 없다고 했어요.

qs.q: What can be inferred about the school on weekends?
o: Students come for extra classes
The classroom is used for a market
The doors are open for visitors
No one is there to care for a pet
qs.why: 주말에는 학교가 문을 닫아(school is closed) 먹이를 줄 사람이 없어요.

qs.q: Why does Ms. Ahn say, "Moving a heavy tank is risky"?
o: She does not accept Dana's offer
She wants to buy a lighter tank
She thinks fish are unsafe pets
She asks Dana to carry it carefully
qs.why: Dana의 제안(매주 금요일 집에 가져가기)에 반대하며 대안으로 급식기를 말해요.

qs.q: In the dialogue, "hardly see it" means
o: see it from far away
clearly see it
almost never see it
easily see it
qs.why: hardly는 거의 ~않는다는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: What will the class probably do next?
o: Wait for next term to decide
Vote on keeping fish with a feeder
Buy two hamsters for the front of the classroom
Take the tank home on Fridays
qs.why: Ms. Ahn이 급식기가 있는 물고기로 투표하자고 제안했어요.

items.title: A Polite No
items.text:
Ines: Hi, Mr. Park. Sorry to bother you. We're going away next weekend, and I wondered if you could look after our dog.
Mr. Park: I'd love to help, Ines, but I'm afraid I can't. Dogs make me sneeze terribly, and I get a rash.
Ines: Oh no, I didn't know that.
Mr. Park: Don't worry. But Sumi at number twelve walks dogs after school. Perhaps they'd like the job.
Ines: Is Sumi reliable?
Mr. Park: Very. Sumi looked after my garden last summer and never forgot once.
Ines: That's good to hear. I'll knock on their door this afternoon.
Mr. Park: Tell Sumi I sent you. And give your dog a pat from me, from a distance!

qs.q: Why is Mr. Park unable to look after the dog?
o: He is afraid of large dogs
He will be away next weekend
His garden needs his attention
Dogs make him sneeze and get a rash
qs.why: 개 때문에 재채기와 발진이 생긴다고 했어요.

qs.q: What can be inferred from Mr. Park's last sentence?
o: He thinks the dog is too noisy
He is angry that Ines asked him
He likes dogs but cannot go near them
He wants to meet the dog next week
qs.why: 'from a distance'라는 농담에서 개를 좋아하지만 가까이 갈 수 없음을 알 수 있어요.

qs.q: Why does Mr. Park bring up Sumi?
o: To complain about a neighbor
To get help with his garden
To ask Ines to hire Sumi's family
To help solve Ines's problem
qs.why: 거절하면서도 대신 부탁할 만한 사람을 소개해 주려는 거예요.

qs.q: In the dialogue, "I'm afraid I can't" means
o: I don't know how to try
I'm sorry, but I cannot
I'm scared to do it
I will do it later
qs.why: I'm afraid ~는 정중하게 유감을 표현하며 거절하는 표현이에요.

qs.q: What will Ines probably do this afternoon?
o: Cancel the trip for the weekend
Walk the dog for an hour
Bring the dog to Mr. Park's house
Visit Sumi to ask about dog care
qs.why: Ines는 오후에 Sumi의 집 문을 두드리겠다고 했어요.

items.title: Which Ticket?
items.text:
Passenger: Hi, one ticket to Lakeside for tomorrow morning, please.
Clerk: The 8:10 express costs twenty-four dollars and arrives at 10:10. The 9:30 local costs seventeen dollars and arrives at 12:30.
Passenger: Why is the difference so big?
Clerk: The express makes only two stops. The local stops at every town.
Passenger: I see. My cousin's graduation starts at noon, and I'll need time to find the hall.
Clerk: Then the express is the safer choice. Are you a student?
Passenger: Yes, I have my ID.
Clerk: Students get ten percent off, so that helps with the price.
Passenger: Wonderful. I'll take it. Could you also tell me which platform to use?
Clerk: Platform three, about ten minutes before departure.

qs.q: When does the local train arrive in Lakeside?
qs.why: 일반 열차는 12시 30분에 도착한다고 했어요.

qs.q: What can be inferred about the local train?
o: It does not run in the morning
It leaves earlier than the express and costs more money
It stops at more places than the express
It is cheaper because it is newer
qs.why: 급행은 두 곳만 서고 완행은 모든 마을에 선다고 했어요.

qs.q: Why does the passenger mention the cousin's graduation?
o: To ask for a discount
To explain a past trip
To show why arrival time matters
To invite the clerk to the event
qs.why: 정오에 시작하는 행사 때문에 도착 시간이 중요하다는 이유를 말하려는 거예요.

qs.q: In the dialogue, the word "express" describes a train that
o: carries only students
is fast and has few stops
is very crowded
stops at every town
qs.why: express는 정차 역이 적은 급행열차를 뜻해요.

qs.q: What will the passenger probably do?
o: Buy the express ticket with a student discount
Go to the hall by bus instead
Choose the local ticket because it costs seventeen dollars
Wait until noon to buy a ticket
qs.why: 급행이 더 안전한 선택이라고 해서 학생 할인으로 급행표를 사요.

items.title: Poster Feedback
items.text:
Mei: Can you look at my poster for the recycling fair? I'm not sure about it.
Sam: Sure. I love the bright green title. You can read it from across the room.
Mei: Thanks! I worked on that for an hour.
Sam: The pictures are great too. But there's a lot of small writing at the bottom. People probably won't stop to read it.
Mei: Hmm, I wanted to include all the facts about plastic.
Sam: Maybe choose three important facts and make them bigger? You could save the rest for a handout.
Mei: That might work. Would the poster look empty then?
Sam: Not if you leave space around the pictures. White space helps the eyes rest.
Mei: Okay, I'll try it tonight and show you again tomorrow.

qs.q: What does Sam suggest doing with the other facts?
o: Writing them around the title
Deleting them completely
Putting them on a handout
Moving them to the pictures
qs.why: 나머지는 유인물(handout)에 담으라고 제안해요.

qs.q: What can be inferred about Mei's first version of the poster?
o: It has more text than passersby will read
It has no pictures at all
It is hard to see from far away
It was finished in one hour
qs.why: 하단에 작은 글씨가 많아 사람들이 읽으려고 멈추지 않을 것이라고 했어요.

qs.q: Why does Sam mention white space?
o: To tell Mei to use a white background
To reassure Mei that fewer words can work
To say the pictures are too big
To suggest a new title color
qs.why: 빈 공간이 눈을 쉬게 해 준다며 글을 줄여도 괜찮다고 안심시키는 말이에요.

qs.q: In the dialogue, "handout" means
o: a place to hang posters
a printed paper given to people
a prize for the best poster
a tool for drawing pictures
qs.why: handout은 나눠 주는 인쇄물이에요.

qs.q: What will Mei do next?
o: Add more facts to the bottom
Change the poster and show Sam again
Ask Sam to redraw the pictures
Throw the poster away and begin a new one with Sam
qs.why: Mei는 오늘 밤 수정해서 내일 다시 보여 주겠다고 했어요.

items.title: Gym or Field?
items.text:
Chae: We need to choose a spot for our game booth at the festival: the gym or the field.
Alex: The field. It's bigger, so we can set up the ring toss.
Chae: But the forecast says rain on Saturday, and there are only four tents for the whole school.
Alex: Hmm. The gym is dry, but the stage is in there, and the music will be loud.
Chae: True. Players wouldn't hear our rules.
Alex: We could make picture signs instead of explaining everything out loud.
Chae: Smart. And we could ask for the corner farthest from the stage.
Alex: Then the gym works. We'd lose some space, though, so we should skip the ring toss.
Chae: Fine. A bean-bag game needs less room anyway.
Alex: I'll draw the signs tonight.

qs.q: What does Chae say about the tents?
o: They will be put up in the gym
Each class has its own tent
There are only four for the whole school
They are too small for a game booth in the field
qs.why: 학교 전체에 텐트가 네 개뿐이라고(only four tents) 말해요.

qs.q: What can be inferred about the ring toss?
o: It was Chae's first idea
It needs more space than a bean-bag game
It is quieter than other games
It is easier to play in the rain than other games
qs.why: 공간이 줄어서 고리 던지기를 빼고 공간을 덜 쓰는 콩주머니 게임을 택해요.

qs.q: Why does Alex suggest picture signs?
o: To save money on paper
To show the weather forecast
To get around the loud music
To decorate the field
qs.why: 음악이 시끄러워 규칙을 말로 전달하기 어려워서 그림 표지판을 제안해요.

qs.q: In "Then the gym works," the word "works" means
o: is working hard
is open for jobs
is a suitable choice
is far from the stage
qs.why: works는 여기서 괜찮은 선택이라는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: What will the class probably do?
o: Run a bean-bag game in the gym, away from the stage
Use the stage for their booth
Choose a different day for the festival
Set up a ring toss on the field
qs.why: 체육관 무대에서 먼 구석에 부스를 만들고 콩주머니 게임을 하기로 했어요.
